title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v125
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: bring the benchmark-lab up to v125 to cover new mixed-workload performance suites, updated profiling baselines for kernel-selection telemetry, representative workload runners for streaming+function-calling scenarios, and an upgraded reporting pipeline that emits per-variant latency/cost histograms. Summary: adds three new test suites (mixed_short, mixed_long, streaming_functions), updates the profiling baselines and baseline ingestion scripts, adds representative workload runners with configurable replay speed and token-distribution presets, and a reporting pipeline job that aggregates p50/p90/p99 latency and cost-per-token per model variant and emits to the nightly reporting table. This PR is intended to improve regression detection for recent kernel changes and adaptive-batching heuristics. Checklist: - [x] Add mixed-workload performance suites and canonical inputs - [x] Update profiling baseline JSONs and ingestion code - [x] Add runners that support function-calling traces and streaming inputs - [x] Wire reporting pipeline to new baseline table and add alerts for regressions - [x] Add unit/integration tests and local replay harness Notes: the description includes config defaults and migration guidance; existing nightly ETL expects the table benchmark_lab.reports_v124, this PR migrates to reports_v125 and provides a compatibility shim for one release. See Linear tasks ENG-725 and ENG-732 for acceptance criteria and perf targets.
commits: feat(bench): add mixed_short and mixed_long performance suites and canonical inputs
feat(bench): add streaming_functions runner with function-calling trace replay
chore(bench): profiling baselines v125 JSON + ingestion migration shim

test(bench): add unit tests for replay speed and token-distribution presets
ci: expand bench CI matrix to include staging cluster run
docs: add migration note and runbook for reports_v125

benchmark-lab/suites/mixed_long.yaml - longer generation templates + conditioning inputs

benchmark-lab/runners/replay_harness.py - update to support configurable replay speed
infra/ci/bench-matrix.yml - add staging benchmark job to CI
docs/benchmark-lab/readme.md - add notes for streaming_function runner
telemetry/kernel_selection/probes_v2.proto - small telemetry probe for kernel selection histograms
telemetry/etl/compute_cost_per_token.py - new helper used by reporting job
examples/bench/quickstart_v125.ipynb - example run for local replay

review_comments: Jordan Li: Left a few nits on the streaming runner interface - prefer explicit backpressure semantics instead of sleep-based pacing. Also please add a comment about deterministic seeding for replayed random choices.
Maya Patel: Responded - switched sleep-based pacing to a token-aware backpressure loop and added deterministic seeding options exposed via CLI flag. Updated tests to assert deterministic outputs.
Evan Brooks: CI runs looked good but found an intermittent failure in test_baseline_ingest on database timeouts. Suggest adding retry with backoff in the ingest shim.
Maya Patel: Added exponential backoff (3 retries) to ingest_baselines.py; re-ran integration CI on staging and it is green.

Priya Nair: Approved after verifying the reporting SQL follows our cost attribution model and the alert thresholds match ENG-725 acceptance criteria. Recommended a follow-up to add dashboard tiles to Redwood Console.
Automated CI Bot: bench-matrix staging job completed successfully (duration ~22m).
release_notes: Add benchmark-lab v125: mixed workload suites, streaming+function-call runners, updated profiling baselines, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates per-variant latency and cost histograms. Includes migration shim for nightly ETL. Improves regression detection for kernel-selection and adaptive-batching changes.
migration_instructions: Nightly ETL: switch scheduled job from benchmark_lab.reports_v124 to benchmark_lab.reports_v125 after deployment. The ingest script includes a compatibility shim; monitor bench_regression_alerts for the first 48h. Dashboards: add tiles using reports_v125.summary_table. See docs/benchmark-lab/migration_v125.md for step-by-step runbook.
notes: This PR was coordinated with infra to provision staging bench capacity for one-off runs. No customer-facing API changes. Follow-up: add Redwood Console dashboard tiles and a periodic smoke test for streaming_function runner in perf canary.
